reason: All three in-scope claims about the float64-based single-rounding epilogue are rebutted by runtime evidence in the highest-risk windows of the public domain. c1 (fp64 product precision loss causing off-by-one outputs for large |a|, small r): rebutted by t9 (0/32768 random large-|a| r=0 samples) and decisively by t15 (0/3200 engineered samples with residuals within ±600 of the exact 2^30 rounding boundary, |P|≈2^61 > 2^53, r=0, odd multipliers near 2^31) — the exact window where a ~2^9 fp64 product error could cross the k+0.5 boundary. c2 (exact halfway cases misrounded): rebutted by t10 (36/36 engineered exact-halfway cases with positive and negative |P|≈2^61 twins all matching the exact integer reference; floor(scaled+0.5) preserves round-half-up since product error ≤2^-22 in scaled units). c3 (denominator shift misbehavior for large r or asymmetric errors at a=-2^31): rebutted by t16 (0/4160 mismatches across r=0..31 including a=-2^31 and a=2^31-1 extreme rows, exact-halfway rows per r, and nonsaturating targets). The earlier c3 probe crash (t11) was a probe-construction bug (non-contiguous transpose), not kernel behavior, and was superseded by the fixed t16 probe. Scope: all claims cite the problem.txt contract requiring exact integer equality (atol=0, rtol=0) over the complete public domain (every int32 accumulator, multipliers [2^30,2^31-1], shifts [0,31]), which the probes directly exercise; the artifact provides no test.py/get_inputs, so problem.txt is the operative contract. The Skeptic reviewed all 16 tool events and recorded no new claims. No confirmed in-scope correctness failure exists; the kernel matches the exact single-rounding reference in every tested adversarial and extreme condition.
